sources.note: Silent on stress placement. Gives segmental inventories for Cateel, Caraga, Manay, Tarragona Mandaya and a section 'The Vowel Lengthening' (lengthened /a:/, /u:/ e.g. /bu:lak/ 'flower', /i:yayas/ 'wild pig'), but no statement on where stress falls.

sources.note: Second-hand/comparative only: sec. 8.10 -- Mansaka shortness and Kalagan length correspond to Bisayan accent but 'in Mansaka and Kalagan these forms are only remnants of a pre-existing system since many forms are unmarked for accent'; fn.70 (p.298) Kamayo preserves PPH accent, Mansaka and Kalagan only relics. Boso and Caraga (Mandaya) forms are cited from Gallman/SIL survey lists without any accent statement.

sources.citation: Svelmoe, Gordon & Thelma Svelmoe. 1974. Notes on Mansaka grammar (Language Data, Asian-Pacific Series 6). Huntington Beach/Ukarumpa: SIL. Ch. 1 'Mansaka background and phonology', pp. 13-15 (Rosetta Project scans rosettaproject_msk_detail-1, rosettaproject_msk_phon-1). SISTER LANGUAGE Mansaka [msk].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For Mansaka (not Mandaya): p.15 'There are 19 phonemes in Mansaka.. Vowel shortness is also phonemic.. not written, since it has a low functional load' with minimal pairs (baga 'lung' / ba(short)ga? 'dwelling'); refers to Abrams 1963. No statement of stress placement. p.13: 'Mansaka, Mandaya, and Mangaragan are mutually intelligible for ordinary purposes'.

sources.note: Only dedicated study of prosody (length vs. stress) in an Eastern Mansakan language; Svelmoe 1974 defers to it; snippet shows it discusses 'Mansaka stress-length' and the Mandaya dialect areas. Sister language, but the closest primary prosodic analysis available for the Mansaka-Mandaya cluster.
